reason: Part of a count ('1 pleat on each side of midrib'). The counted part is the pleat (fold), and the midrib (leaf midvein PO_0020139) only says where. 'each side' and 'per side' were rejected before as not plant structures.
Narrower: a hair, which PO lists as a synonym of trichome. 'Feathery' is the quality plumose (PATO_0005010, synonym feathery) and should be split off as the quality, not kept in the bearer.
A count phrase. The counted part is flower (PO_0009046) and 'per cycle' is the unit it is counted in. 'cycle', 'per whorl' and 'leaves per whorl' were rejected before for the same reason.

A relative length ('1/2-3/4 length of petal spur'), so pattern 10 (ratio to another part). The petal spur (floral spur FLOPO_0986133) is the part it is compared with, not the bearer. Same as 'fraction of leaf' and 'calyx length'.

Narrower: a papilla that secretes. This follows C269/C391, where 'papilla' and 'papillae' went to papilla cell. 'Glandular' is the quality and should be split off. On stipules these may be small multicellular glands; if so, portion of secretory tissue (PO_0005656) would be the better class.
The plural of 'glandular papilla' and decided the same way. It is narrower than papilla cell, with 'glandular' as the quality.
A count phrase ('1–10 per branch'). 'head' already goes to capitulum inflorescence (PO_0030121, C262), and 'per branch' is the unit of the count, like 'per node' and 'per head'.

The second term of a ratio ('proximal inflorescence bract 1/2-... inflorescence length'), so pattern 10. The bearer is the bract and inflorescence (PO_0009049) is the part it is compared with. Same as 'leaf length' and 'seed length'.

target: pappus (PO_0025393): count of its elements, inner series via the context word inner (FLOPO_0991378); subulate (PATO_0001954) as the quality
reason: This is how Flora of North America describes Asteraceae pappi ('20+ outer scales or bristles ... inner subulate scales or bristles'). It counts the inner pappus elements, which fits pattern 03 with the pappus as the whole. Limit the rule to pappus/Asteraceae context: 'scale' and 'bristle' alone were rejected as generic.
Small teeth between the main teeth of an unnamed organ (a calyx, as in Lythraceae, or a leaf margin). 'tooth' needs its organ, and 'interstitial' was rejected as a fragment before.

A nectary on an involucel. Both classes exist and 'part of a qualified whole' can express it, with presence and absence through pattern 15. If the source actually means cyathium involucre glands, the whole should be involucre (PO_0009100) and not involucel. Check one record.
'ridge' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ (2026-11-13). 'lateral rib' and 'lateral keel' were rejected for the same reason, and 'Lateral' does not supply the organ.
'blade with 4 orders of leaflets' gives how many times a compound leaf is divided. That is a quality of the leaf (compound leaf), not a structure, as with 'orders of branching'.

Two kinds of part joined as alternatives ('leaflets/lobes 11–23'): leaflet (PO_0020049) for compound leaves and leaf lobes for lobed ones. A single rule would ground one of them wrongly. Same as 'teeth or lobe'.
A count phrase. The counted part is the leaf and the caudex (stem PO_0009047, C252) is the unit, as with 'per caudex branch' and 'per node'.
The reference term of a relative length or position ('widest at 0.4–0.55 length of body'), so pattern 10. 'body' alone was rejected as a generic part.

Narrower. In these floras 'major' and 'minor' spines are the two ranks of areole spines in cacti ('major spines (0-)1-5'), and areole spines are modified leaves. 'major' is a rank, like 'primary'. If the rule fires outside cactus descriptions, demote it to rejected, as with 'spine tip'.

Spines on the margin of an unnamed organ: spiny leaf-margin teeth (Agave, Eryngium, thistles) or phyllary appendages. These are not spine leaves. The organ is missing, as with 'lateral spine' and 'basal spine'.
'rib' was rejected as a generic part that needs its organ, and 'median lobe' and 'lateral rib' were rejected the same way. 'median ribs 3' does not say whose ribs they are.

A generic word for a member of any whorl ('perianth members 6', '7-9-merous'), like the French 'pièce', which was rejected. Perianth members are tepals (PO_0009033), but the word alone also counts floral members of any whorl. '-merous' is a whorl count of the organ named.
Narrower. This is the second rank of cactus areole spines ('minor spines (0-)5-11'); decided the same way as 'major spine'.

A count phrase ('2–8 nodes between branches'). The counted part is stem node (PO_0020141, rule C254 on 'node'), and 'between branch' gives the stretch of stem being counted, which the patterns do not hold. It is not a structure.

target: pappus (PO_0025393): count of its elements, outer series via the context word outer (FLOPO_0991379)
reason: The outer pappus elements in Asteraceae ('outer scales or bristles 20+'), the pair of 'inner subulate scales or bristle'. Pattern 03 with the pappus as the whole. Limit it to pappus context, because 'scale' and 'bristle' alone are generic.
The unit of a count ('areoles 8-10 per diagonal across midstem segment' in Opuntia). The counted part is the areole, and the phrase is not a structure. Same as 'per areole' and 'per segment'.
Two count units joined by 'or' ('1 per node or 2-5 per cluster'). 'per node' and 'per cluster' were both rejected as not plant structures.
Hairs on the Carex perigynium. Both classes exist, so 'part of a qualified whole' can express it. Use the perigynium class PO_0009044, not the 'perigynium' synonym on involucral bract.

The second term of a relative width ('1/2 to nearly equaling petal claw width'), so pattern 10. 'claw' alone was rejected as a generic part. Here the organ is the petal (PO_0009032), but it is only the part compared with.
The second term of a relative width ('1/3–2/3 petal width'), so pattern 10 with petal (PO_0009032) as the part compared with. Same as 'leaf width' and 'calyx length'.
A quality: plicate (PATO_0104365, synonym pleated). '5-plicate' is a count of the folds of the organ described (pattern 03), as decided for 'plicae'. It is not a structure.

A wrong lemma of the suffix '-porate' ('Pollen mostly 4-porate'). The bearer is pollen (PO_0025281) and the value is its number of pores, like 'celled' and 'ribbed'. A flora_counted_parts.tsv entry (porate -> pore on pollen) is the fix. 'pore' alone was rejected as generic.
